Rye Loaf Baker's Percentage

Detailed method

The calculator opens at 450 g flour, 80% hydration, 2.2% salt, and 1.2% yeast. Rye will not feel like a stretchy wheat dough. Mix it, pan it, and bake it through. Seeds pressed on the top, if you add them, are extra and are not in the gram total. The balls fields open at 1 loaf of about 825 g. These times assume you only change the flour amount and keep the percentages the same. Still judge the dough by how it looks and feels.

  1. Mix Stir the flour, water, salt, and yeast until no dry flour remains. The dough is sticky and will not pull a windowpane. Aim for about 26°C (79°F).
  2. Rest Cover the bowl for 20 minutes so the flour drinks the water.
  3. Pan Oil a loaf pan. Scrape the dough in and smooth the top with a wet hand. Do not try to shape a tight ball.
  4. Seeds Press seeds onto the wet top if you want them. They are not part of the gram total.
  5. Proof Cover the pan at about 26°C (79°F) for 45 to 70 minutes. With 1.2% yeast it should rise to just under the rim. It will not double like white dough.
  6. Bake Heat the oven to 200°C (390°F). Bake 20 minutes, then lower to 180°C (355°F) and bake 30 to 40 minutes more, until the sides are firm. If you check the center, look for about 96°C (205°F).
  7. Cool Turn it out and cool it on a rack for at least 8 hours before you slice. Cut earlier and the crumb smears.
